minutes.headline: Committee kept the drop-grade-one, 3% grid option alive but deferred a final grid vote to Wednesday.
minutes.summary: The committee compared FY24 and FY25 salary grid scenarios ahead of the town meeting warrant. The first option (drop one step, add one, 3%) kept solid support, and a new option starting at step three was held for pricing. It agreed on several outlier grade changes and set the police executive assistant at grade 10. It also debated sick leave for non-birthing parents and adoption, and left the number of days to be settled Wednesday.

attendees.role: staff who prices the grid scenarios (HR/finance)

public_comment.topic: Nancy said vacation and personal time should be used before sick time for non-birthing parent leave.
Pauline asked whether the vacation policy would go on the warrant. She was told there was not enough time and it would be looked at for the fall town meeting.

votes.motion: Set the police executive assistant position at grade 10.

budget_items.topic: Grid option: drop grade one step one, 3%
budget_items.what_was_said: The first option was costed with the sewer enterprise and formula grant portions removed. It adds a 3% increase on top of the 2.5% grid move already given.

budget_items.topic: Grid option starting at 1530 in grade one step one
budget_items.what_was_said: A second option was costed higher than the first. It was set aside in favour of a new option starting at 1550.

budget_items.topic: Option dropping grade one and starting grade two at 1550
budget_items.what_was_said: This option was described as low cost because few people move up.

budget_items.topic: FY25 impact of further market adjustment
budget_items.what_was_said: Members estimated that a second adjustment in FY25 could cost roughly double the first. A phased approach over two years was suggested.
Clerical employees received a retroactive adjustment as their first increase for the prior year, which was compared with the committee's own grid moves.

decisions.decision: The first grid option and Julie's new option (grade one at 1550) are held as the two finalists, with both to be priced for Wednesday.
Agreed to recommend moving the library pages to grade two, the COA meal site manager from six to seven, and the COA outreach coordinator from seven to eight.
The pack manager grade is to be worked on further before Wednesday, with a move to about 12 to 14 under discussion.
No vote is needed on the job description framework. The committee will use the 12-characteristics format going forward.
The FMLA sick-leave language will be written up for the warrant, with the number of days to be finalised Wednesday.
The vacation policy will not be on this warrant and will be looked at for the fall town meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee held two salary grid options as finalists and set both to be priced for a decision on Wednesday.
The committee agreed to recommend grade changes for the library pages, the COA meal site manager and the COA outreach coordinator.
A vote set the police executive assistant position at grade 10; the result of the vote is not audible in the recording.
Sick-leave language for non-birthing parents and adoption will be written for the warrant, with the number of days left for Wednesday.
The vacation policy will not go on this warrant and will be taken up for the fall town meeting.

why_it_matters: The grid option chosen sets the pay scale for town employees and feeds the FY25 personnel line that residents vote on at town meeting.
The sick-leave language and grade changes are headed for the warrant, so residents will be asked to vote on them as articles.
watch_next: Wednesday's Personnel Committee meeting: the final grid vote, the number of sick-leave days, and the pack manager grade.
The fall town meeting, where the vacation policy is expected to be taken up.
